beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier around a compact recurrent thought process, then decodes the updated field.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image field from the compact computation that updates it. The encoder first maps the low-resolution input into features. The window step partitions that dense field for local processing. DQ-CTM runs repeated thought ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into a super-resolved image. The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, so the whole image path is not repeated.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks
params.note: The loop belongs to the thought stage, not the whole pipeline.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features, and windowing partitions that field while preserving its tokens.
beats.narration: The equation defines the dense carrier that the thought process reads and updates. The low-resolution image is the input being lifted into feature space. The encoder produces the dense feature field. The feature field is the persistent carrier. The window partition forms the token set without dropping the carrier.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed

terms.label: encoder that makes the dense feature field
window partition that keeps every token

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the cheapest model in the reported benchmark; its parameter count is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The reported parameter counts put the transformer baseline CATANet at the smallest size. RFDN and IMDN are also smaller than DQ-CTM-SR. DQ-CTM-SR uses one point one two nine million parameters, the second largest count here. CARN is the largest model in this comparison.
